title: Referrals and repeat work from existing clients for bond and end-of-lease cleaning
audience: Owners of bond and end-of-lease cleaning businesses who want referrals and repeat work from the agents, property managers and tenants they have served.
learningOutcomes: Plan a review or referral request that is made after the client confirms the result and that the client can decline easily.
Write a next-service offer with a date, a scope and a price approach, and schedule the check-in that follows it.
Write referral reward terms, including the condition for payment, before any referral is made.

instruction.heading: Ask once the agent has confirmed the clean
instruction.body: Ask for a review or a referral after the agent or tenant has confirmed the clean matches the agreed list, usually at handover or when the invoice is paid. Do not ask before the result is confirmed, and do not tie the ask to any bond outcome you do not control. Use one sentence, name the next step, and make it easy to decline. One Baylor Keller Center experiment found that a late reminder drew more reviews than an immediate one; that is one experiment only. The AMA says timing depends on the product.

instruction.heading: Ask every client, and use the review link
instruction.body: Google provides a review link or QR code that you can share. Ask every client, not only the ones you expect to praise. Filtering who is asked is review gating, which the vendor Podium says Google treats as a violation (not checked against Google's policy). Never write reviews for clients or invent them. Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews, and the ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says (15 July 2026).

instruction.heading: Offer the next job before the agent leaves
instruction.body: Bond cleaning is a one-off for each tenancy, so repeat work usually comes from an agent or property manager who handles many exits. At handover, propose a next job with a date, scope and price approach, such as a clean for the next vacancy across the agent's portfolio. The timing is an illustrative choice, not a sourced benchmark. Get written confirmation before you change the schedule. A short follow-up after each completed job is one approach vendors recommend (Housecall Pro, 8 June 2026); if it promotes a service by email or text, check the ACMA rules first.

instruction.heading: Set referral rewards in writing before anyone refers
instruction.body: Decide the reward and write the payment condition, usually that the referred party has booked and completed a paid job. Stating the referrer's reward in the invitation increased referrals across the studies that Xu, Yu and Tu report (2023). Get the referred person's consent before any message goes to them, because the referrer's word alone may not be enough (Clayton Utz, 2017, older source). Referral fees or gifts to agents are a gap in the research: check the agent's own rules and get advice before paying anything.

instruction.heading: Re-contact only those who can still be served
instruction.body: Tenants move on, so a tenant is rarely a repeat client. Re-contact agents and property managers on a short factual schedule, and offer only the slots you can deliver. Keep the message optional. Honour every opt-out within five working days (ACMA).

procedure: After each handover is signed off, make one review or referral request, and record what was asked and the answer.
Write the next-job offer with a date, scope, interval and price approach, and get written confirmation.
Set referral terms and the payment condition before the first referral is made.
Check any referral message for consent, and send electronic messages only under the ACMA rules.
When a referral books and is paid, apply the reward and record the outcome.
Review each season which requests, offers and timings produced repeat work.

workedExamples.situation: [ILLUSTRATIVE] A bond cleaner has completed three move-outs for one property manager. At the last handover the manager says a colleague at another agency could use the same service, and asks what she would get for the introduction.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the cleaner write down before the colleague is contacted, and what should be avoided?
workedExamples.reasoning: The cleaner writes the referral terms first: what the introducer receives, the condition for payment (for example, a paid move-out for the colleague), and when the reward is applied. The cleaner asks the manager to pass on the colleague's details, and contacts the colleague only after that person agrees. The cleaner does not promise a payment that is not written, does not tie any reward to what a review says, and does not offer anything in exchange for a review. If the reward is cash or a credit, the cleaner checks its tax and contract effect with an adviser. The cleaner also checks the agency's rules on referral payments, which the research did not cover.

equipmentAndPpe: Client record with the sign-off date and the review or referral request made
Next-service offer template with scope, interval and price approach
Calendar of seasonal re-contact dates for the service
No PPE is needed for client follow-up; any site visit follows the site's own safety rules

commonErrors.error: Asking for a review before the agent has confirmed the clean.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask at handover or after payment, once the result is confirmed.

commonErrors.error: Offering a referral reward that was never written down.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the reward and its payment condition before any referral, and give the referrer a copy.

commonErrors.error: Filtering which agents or tenants are asked for a review.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask every client, and let the review link do the rest.

commonErrors.error: Promising a pass or a bond refund as a reason to refer or review.
commonErrors.prevention: Speak only to the clean you delivered and the list you agreed.

commonErrors.error: Contacting a client who asked not to hear from you.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep an opt-out list and act on each request within five working days.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Publishing a client's name, photo, review or property detail needs the client's consent for that use. Property details can be personal information. If the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) applies to your business, check the OAIC direct-marketing guidance (modified 5 September 2024). Whether the Act applies was not confirmed.

Check-in and re-contact messages by email or text can be commercial electronic messages under the Spam Act 2003 (Cth). A message that promotes any service can be commercial even when framed as a reminder (Clayton Utz, 2023).
Review platforms and referral schemes have their own rules on incentives. Check each platform's rules, and the ACCC's statement that incentives must be disclosed, before offering any reward.

A referral does not extend the licence or insurance of the business that accepts the work. Accept only work your licence and insurance cover, in the state or territory where the work is done. Licence rules for bond cleaning were not researched.

qualityStandard: Every review or referral request is made after sign-off or payment, and it includes an easy way to decline.
Every next-service offer is written, has a date and is confirmed by the client before the schedule changes.
Every referral reward has written terms and a payment condition, and is paid only when that condition is met.
documentationEvidence: Review or referral request log with the date sent and the answer.
Next-service offers with the date, scope, interval and client confirmation.
Referral reward terms with the referral record and payment outcome.
summary: Ask for reviews and referrals after the agent has confirmed the clean, and make it easy to decline.
Offer the next job in writing, with a date, before the agent leaves.
Write referral terms and payment conditions before anyone refers. Gaps: agent referral channels, referral fees and tenant-level repeat rates were not sourced.

knowledgeChecks.question: When is the best time to ask an agent for a review or referral?
options: Before the clean starts, so the agent feels committed
After the agent has confirmed the clean matches the agreed list
Only after the agent has made a complaint

knowledgeChecks.question: A tenant wants to post a review with their name and a photo of the empty flat. What do you need?
options: The tenant's consent for that name and photo
Nothing, because the review is positive
Your own view that the photo looks good

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a referral reward look like?
options: Paid to anyone who mentions your name
Decided after the referred party books, based on how keen the referrer seems
Written in advance, with the payment condition stated

sourceReferences: Baylor Keller Center, 'Wait Just a Minute', https://kellercenter.hankamer.baylor.edu/news/story/2024/wait-just-minute-when-ask-online-reviews, 1 June 2024 (metadata says 13 May 2024). One experiment only. Supports: an immediate reminder reduced reviews and a later reminder raised them.

American Marketing Association, 'Asking for customer reviews at the right time', https://www.ama.org/2023/01/10/asking-for-customer-reviews-at-the-right-time-sooner-is-not-always-better/, 10 January 2023. Supports: the right timing depends on the product; experience goods need more time to evaluate.

Google Help, Business Profile review help page, https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474122?hl=en-GB, no date shown. Supports: a review link or QR code may be shared; discounts or goods in exchange for reviews are banned.

Podium, 'Review gating', https://www.podium.com/article/review-gating, 2 May 2022. Vendor source; its account of Google's position was not checked against Google's policy. Supports: filtering who is asked for a review is called review gating.

ACCC, 'Online reviews for product and services', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/advertising-and-promotions/online-reviews-for-product-and-services, published and updated 15 July 2026. Supports: incentives for reviews must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says.

ACMA, 'Avoid sending spam', https://www.acma.gov.au/avoid-sending-spam, no date shown; read 2026-11-04 per the research file. Supports: consent, accurate sender details, and an unsubscribe honoured within five working days.

Housecall Pro, 'Recurring service agreements', https://www.housecallpro.com/resources/recurring-service-agreements/, published 8 June 2026, updated 9 June 2026. Vendor source; no statistics used. Supports: a short follow-up after each completed job about a maintenance plan; define in the contract how unused visits roll over.

Xu, Yu and Tu, Journal of Marketing Research 60(2), 2023, https://research.polyu.edu.hk/en/publications/i-will-get-a-reward-too-when-disclosing-the-referrer-reward-incre/. Supports: stating the referrer's reward in the invitation increased referring across the studies reported. No figures used.

Clayton Utz, 'Referrer beware', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2017/may/referrer-beware-proceed-with-caution-when-contemplating-refer-a-friend-promotions, 11 May 2017 (older than 2022). Supports: a referrer's word alone may not be enough; get the referred person's consent.

Clayton Utz, 'The ACMA cranks up enforcement', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2023/november/the-acma-cranks-up-enforcement-do-your-factual-customer-emails-pass-the-spam-act-test, 9 November 2023. Supports: a service reminder that promotes any service can be a commercial message.

OAIC, 'Direct marketing', https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy/privacy-guidance-for-organisations-and-government-agencies/organisations/direct-marketing, published 1 May 2019, modified 5 September 2024. Supports: APP 7 governs direct marketing using personal information; opt-out must be simple.

Notes: no source in the research covers agent referral channels or referral fees (gap). The Baylor result is from one experiment. Podium is a vendor source. The Xu et al. study is not a cleaning study and no figures are used from it.

officialReferences.title: Avoid sending spam
officialReferences.covers: Says commercial messages cannot be sent without the recipient's permission or consent; messages must accurately identify the sender and include correct contact details; every commercial message must contain an unsubscribe option under the Spam Act 2003, which the page says sets out responsibilities under Australian law. Does not mention one-to-one messages. Publisher: ACMA.
